post.description:
Exchanges the OAuth `code` (returned by Google's redirect) for an ID token, verifies the JWT signature + claims, and upserts the user row. Returns the sanitized identity for client-side session state.

**Domain whitelist** is enforced inside JWT-claim validation — non-NEU emails get 401 (PLAN §3.5: split-on-`@` exact match, NOT substring; `attacker@husky.neu.edu.evil.com` is rejected).

**F1 compliance**: no payment surface, no commercialization. The Google client must be set up under the developer's personal Google Cloud project — credentials never enter version control.

**Session** (R2a): `"session": "token"` (the default) returns the signed token as `session_token`, as before. `"session": "cookie"` sets it instead as the HttpOnly cookie `__Host-nc_api_session` (Secure, Path=/, SameSite=Lax, as long as the token lasts) and returns `session_token: null`; the web front end uses this. The cookie mode must come from an allowed web origin with `X-NEU-Compass: 1`, or it gets the fixed CSRF 403 before the code is exchanged: a page elsewhere must not log the browser into an account of its choosing.

**redirect_uri** (R2b): the address Google sent the browser back to, which Google checks again in the exchange; it defaults to `GOOGLE_OAUTH_REDIRECT_URI`. The cookie mode takes only the front end's own address, the request's `Origin` (one in `WEB_ORIGINS`) followed by `/`, and answers 422 to anything else before the code is exchanged.

401.description: Code exchange failed, JWT invalid, or email domain not in whitelist (`husky.neu.edu` / `northeastern.edu`). Besides the fixed `detail`, the body has `reason` (R2b): `token_exchange_rejected`, `token_endpoint_unreachable`, `missing_id_token`, `id_token_invalid`, `claims_invalid`, `email_unverified` or `domain_not_allowed`.

403.description: The cookie mode, not from an allowed web origin with `X-NEU-Compass: 1`.

422.description: The body is malformed, or the cookie mode's `redirect_uri` is not the request's own `Origin` followed by `/`.

post.summary: Google OAuth code → JWT verify → user upsert

post.description: Requires `Authorization: Bearer <session_token>` (or the API's session cookie, R2a) and the body `{"confirm": "delete"}`. In one transaction removes the Co-op experiences this account published (and every unlock of them); then a group it helped publish that is left with one contributor goes back to approved (k=2; no credit is taken back); then the users row, which cascades to its unlocks, planned courses, Co-op submissions and credits. query_log and saved answers never record an account and are not touched; daily backups keep a copy for up to 14 days. Afterwards the same token gets 401 from `/auth/me`. A session cookie used for the call is expired, and so is one that no longer works (with the 401). Returns per-table counts only.

200.description: Deleted; counts of the rows removed.

401.description: Missing, invalid or expired token, or the account no longer exists.

post.summary: Delete the caller's account and Co-op contributions (batch T)

get.description: Builds the Google OAuth address with the caller's `state`, exactly as the Streamlit login link does (`api.google_oauth.authorize_url`). The front end makes `state`, keeps it, and checks it when Google sends the browser back with `?code=&state=`; then it posts the code to `/auth/callback` with `"session": "cookie"` and the same `redirect_uri`. Google sends the browser back to `redirect_uri`, which must be a web front end's own address, an origin in `WEB_ORIGINS` followed by `/` (R2b); without it, to `GOOGLE_OAUTH_REDIRECT_URI`. The API stores nothing here.

200.description: The address to send the browser to.

422.description: `state` is not 16–128 characters of A–Z, a–z, 0–9, `_` or `-`, or `redirect_uri` is not a web front end's own address.

503.description: Login is not configured here (no Google client ID or secret, or no SESSION_SECRET).

get.summary: Google's login address for the web front end (R2a)

post.description: Expires the API's session cookie and answers 204, also when there is none. Bearer tokens are not revoked (they expire on their own; Streamlit logs out by dropping its copy). It must come from an allowed web origin with `X-NEU-Compass: 1`, with or without the cookie, or it gets the fixed CSRF 403 and expires nothing: a page elsewhere must not log the browser out.

204.description: The session cookie, if any, is expired.

403.description: Not from an allowed web origin with `X-NEU-Compass: 1`.

get.description:
Verifies the `Authorization: Bearer <session_token>` credential and returns the current identity from the users table. The UI calls this on page load to restore login state from a persisted cookie — the token signature + max-age are re-checked server-side on every call, so a stale or tampered cookie degrades to 401, never a forged identity.

Without an Authorization header, the API's own session cookie (`__Host-nc_api_session`, set by the cookie mode of `/auth/callback`) is used instead. When that cookie no longer works (bad, expired, or its account is gone), the 401 also expires it.

401.description: Missing, invalid, or expired token — or the token's user row no longer exists.

get.summary: Identity behind the Bearer session token or the session cookie

post.description:
Streams a Gemini-generated answer grounded in the retrieved courses.

**Wire format**: `application/x-ndjson` — one JSON object per newline. Object types in order:

1. `{"type": "meta", "matched_via": "alias|hybrid|empty", "retrieval_ms": float, "results": [{course_id, primary_code, primary_name, score, answer_evidence}, ...], prompt_version, notices?}` — emitted first so the client can render evidence bubbles before tokens land. `notices` appears only when non-empty, e.g. `program_schedule_unverified`: a first-semester/foundational question for a family whose version-scoped rules carry no verified schedule was answered from hybrid retrieval instead of a guessed sequence.
2. `{"type": "token", "text": "..."}` — zero or more, Gemini stream chunks.
3. `{"type": "error", "error_type": "upstream_error|no_answer|internal_error|daily_limit", "detail": "..."}` — only on stream failure, or `daily_limit` instead of tokens when today's model calls are used up (`MODEL_DAILY_CALL_LIMIT`). `detail` is fixed text, never the exception; the server log line carries the same `x-request-id`.
4. `{"type": "done", "feedback": {answer_id, answer_sha256, feedback_token}}` — always last; feedback is optional and issued only after a complete, non-empty answer and successful private storage. Never in meta. Receipt authorizes only this answer's latest vote via `POST /feedback`.

Context, exact aliases, and program shortcuts apply explicit filters before top-k. Hybrid candidates use the same reranker/rejection policy as `/search`, including queries with a program prefix. Answer evidence distinguishes archived catalog snapshots, extracted field quotes, unverified provenance and explicit data gaps; it is not a live catalog verification.

200.description: NDJSON event stream. See description for shape.

409.description: Program selection is ambiguous or conflicts with the query's program prefix.

get.description: `answer_feedback_enabled`: whether to show the opt-in and the votes. `login_available`: Google's client ID and secret and a SESSION_SECRET are all configured, so `/auth/login-url` and the cookie login work (the same condition as login-url's 503).
get.summary: What the web front end needs to know about this API (R2a)

get.description:
Returns curated seeds and reviewed UGC with at least two distinct contributors; applies tier-gated FIELD redaction server-side (PLAN §6.4):

- tier 0 (anonymous / no contributions): company, role, term, industry, duration visible; interview/technical/salary `null`.
- tier 1 (contribution_count ≥ 1): + `interview_summary`, `technical_questions`.
- tier 2 (contribution_count ≥ 2): + `salary_range_usd`.

`visibility_level` reports the row's intrinsic tier (from content presence), so clients can render 'contribute to unlock' hints for redacted fields.

Each row is sanitized: `contributor_user_id` and `redaction_audit` are server-internal and NOT returned.

Before the v1.3 moderation migration the list degrades to curated seeds (public browsing never 503s); the `X-Coop-Moderation` header reports `available` or `missing` so deploy checks can still detect an unapplied migration. Uploads still require the schema.

200.description: Eligible public Co-op records (redacted per tier).

post.description: Authenticated uploads are accepted into a PRIVATE pending queue, not published. A curator must supply reviewed/redacted content; publication requires at least two distinct authenticated contributors with the same company/role/term. Seeds and repeat submissions cannot establish this threshold. Contribution credit is awarded only once per contributor/reviewed group at publication. Retries return the existing submission without replacing its content. 'accepted' means stored, NOT publicly visible; 'status' reports the review state. visibility_level is content-derived; contributor identity comes from a signed Bearer session.

201.description: Private submission stored, or existing submission returned.

401.description: Missing, invalid, expired token, or unknown user.

503.description: Moderation schema has not been migrated.

post.summary: Collect a private Co-op submission for review

get.description:
Returns the rehydrated Pydantic Course (schema v1.1, see `schemas/course.py`). Includes soft fields (workload, difficulty, skill_tags, career_relevance, controversial_signals) **with their evidence_snippets** when present — the UI's evidence-bubble component uses these for source-quote display.

Additionally resolves the Layer 3 ontology context: `program_context` (programs whose curriculum lists this course) and `prerequisites` (prereq edges with display names). Both are `[]` for courses outside any seeded program.

Co-op data is **not** mixed in; call `GET /coop?course_id=...` separately so visibility-tier authorization stays in one place. `answer_evidence` adds recorded catalog provenance, extracted field quotes, missing fields and source/seed warnings; no raw_text is automatically labeled official. `course_requisites` lists year-scoped clause documents separately; literal credit_hours preserve fixed/fractional/range title evidence without choosing section credits or changing the Course integer field. description keyword evidence is not an interpreted enrollment rule. Read-time program_contexts include only same-edition source-checked plans explicitly naming the course, not personal applicability or merged grades. No edition/path is auto-selected and legacy edges remain unverified.
get.summary: Get full Course detail (+ program context)

get.description: Always 200 if the process responds — does **not** check whether the embedder/reranker have warmed. Use `/ready` for that. Suitable for Cloudflare Tunnel / docker / systemd healthcheck.

The sections of the privacy page (heading and plain-text sentences, in page order), the note on what an account deletion removes, and the two notices next to the ask box. Built from this API's QUERY_LOG_RETENTION_DAYS, ANSWER_FEEDBACK_ENABLED and PRIVACY_CONTACT_EMAIL; `capture_notice` is null while answer feedback is off. The front end adds its own pointer to the page after `query_log_notice`.
get.summary: The 数据与隐私 page, from the API's own settings (R2a)

get.description:
Returns every seeded program with its required-course edge count. Public read, not gated content. Legacy seeds have unverified scope; plan_count counts usable version-scoped documents, not verified full degrees.

`course_count` counts curriculum EDGES (including edges whose course hasn't been scraped yet), so it can exceed the number of rows the curriculum view renders.

Returns one program's required courses grouped by `semester_recommended`, display names resolved from the catalog in a single batched SELECT.

Groups are ordered semester 1, 2, ... with the no-recommendation group (`semester: null` — no semester information, NOT anytime eligibility) last. Edges whose course_id is missing from the `courses` table (dangling seed edge, course not yet scraped) are silently dropped rather than failing the whole curriculum view.
get.summary: Program curriculum grouped by recommended semester

get.description: Missing, stale or unusable policy sources return explicit states with no usable fragments. No latest-edition fallback, auto-fetch, DB writes or merged policy decisions.

get.description:
Returns `status='ready'` once the lifespan startup hook completed: FAISS index loaded, BM25 corpus built, bge-m3 embedder warmed, optional reranker warmed when enabled. Returns HTTP 503 with `status='warming'` while the retrieval stack is unavailable (~70-100 seconds of cold model load — see [PLAN_v2.0 §2.5](docs/PLAN_v2.0.md)).

HTTP 200 means ready. Orchestrators must not route user traffic on HTTP 503; `/health` remains the process-liveness endpoint.

Turns a shareable course reference into internal `course_id`s so the UI can open a `?course=` deep link.

Accepted forms: internal id (`neu-cs-5800`), canonical code with any URL separator (`CS-5800`, `CS_5800`, `CS+5800`, `CS 5800`), the space-free spelling (`cs5800`), and any **approved** alias (`Algo`) — the same `v_course_lookup` view `/search`'s alias stage uses, so `review_status='pending'` aliases are excluded.

Always 200. An unresolvable ref returns `matches: []` — a dead link is a normal outcome, not an error. `matches` may hold more than one course when the ref is ambiguous.

**Not** logged to `query_log`: deep-link resolution is machine traffic and must not contaminate organic-query telemetry.

200.description: Resolution ran. `matches` is ordered most-specific first and is `[]` when nothing matched.

get.summary: Resolve a deep-link course reference to course_ids

post.description:
Production search path. Three-stage pipeline:

1. **Alias resolution** — `query_normalizer` strips/lowercases the query and looks it up in `v_course_lookup` (which excludes `review_status='pending'` aliases). On hit, returns immediately with `matched_via='alias'`, score=1.0. Covers `'CS 5800'` / `'cs5800'` / `'Algo'` / `'应用 AI'`.
2. **Hybrid retrieval** — BM25 (110 stopwords filtered) + bge-m3 vector via Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF, k=60). Hard filters apply at SQLite layer; only `status='indexed'` rows surface (ADR-0013).
3. **Rerank + Z-score blend + reject** (PLAN v2.2 §3.4 + §3.5) — single bge-reranker-v2-m3 pass over the candidate pool. If `max(raw_sigmoid) < 0.05` (ADR-0016): `matched_via='rejected'`, empty results, populated `rejection_reason`. Otherwise α=0.4 Z-score blend (ADR-0015) reorders the top-5 and returns `matched_via='hybrid'`.

**Latency budget**: alias path ~3ms, hybrid+rerank ~50ms p50 post-warmup.

200.description: Search resolved. `matched_via` ∈ {alias, hybrid, empty, rejected}. `results=[]` when matched_via is empty or rejected; `rejection_reason` is non-null only when rejected.

422.description: Invalid request (empty query, k out of range, unknown delivery_mode, extra unknown fields).
